questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1 Scene 1, who stops the servants' brawl?
questions.why: Benvolio tries to break up the servants' fight; Tybalt instead arrives and escalates it, which is a common mix-up.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In the progression C-Am-F-G, which chord is built on the sixth scale degree?
questions.why: Am is the 'vi' chord, built on the sixth note of the C major scale. Students often confuse it with F (the 'IV', fourth degree) or G (the 'V', fifth degree).

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: In Paint Like a Beast, what tool did students use besides brushes to apply paint?
questions.why: Students used sponges and rags alongside brushes to build texture, not rulers or tape, which would create unwanted sharp, precise edges.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these groups in Japan's feudal system by how much rice they typically produced through their own labour, from most to least
questions.why: Peasants farmed the land and produced the rice; daimyo, samurai, and the shogun lived off rice collected as tax rather than growing it themselves.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these stages of tracing continuity and change, from first to last
sequence: Pick a starting point in time
Pick a later point in time
Decide what changed and what stayed the same
questions.why: Tracing change starts by fixing two points in time, comparing them, then deciding what actually shifted versus what continued unchanged.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1 Scene 1, what does the Prince threaten if the families fight in the streets again?
questions.why: Prince Escalus declares that any further street brawling between the Capulets and Montagues will be punished by death, raising the stakes for the rest of the play.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What genre is Romeo and Juliet classed as?
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy, a play centred on a hero's downfall that ends in death. Students sometimes call it a history play or comedy because it has light early scenes, but the genre is fixed by its tragic ending.
